title: introduce-kms-residency-proof-validator-and-rbac-residency-assertions
author: Ravi Patel
release_notes: Adds a validator that enforces KMS key residency proofs on tenant-scoped requests and plumbs new RBAC predicates for residency-aware role checks. No behavioral changes by default; feature gated behind 'residency_proofs' feature flag.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR implements a runtime check that validates a tenant-level KMS residency proof attached to requests that perform cross-region key unwrap/wrap operations. The goal is to provide cryptographic proof (signed assertion) that a CMK is resident in an allowed jurisdiction before the request is allowed to use that key. This complements existing geo-routing and audit pipelines by preventing accidental cross-border crypto operations for tenants with residency constraints.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a KMS residency proof validator component (pkg/security/residency/validator) that verifies signed proofs against a local trust bundle and returns an enum: VALID | EXPIRED | INVALID | MISSING.
- Introduces new RBAC predicate attributes (rbac.residency_allowed and rbac.residency_denied) and wiring in the policy evaluator to short-circuit evaluates based on residency checks.
- Extends audit logs with a residency_verification field (enum) and a compact proof reference (sha256) instead of embedding entire provenance. Audit records include residency outcome and validator version to enable post-hoc compliance audits without leaking full keys.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag 'residency_proofs' and default-off for older clusters.

Implementation notes / commits summary:
- Commit 1: scaffold residency validator, minimal interface, unit tests for proof parsing and signature verification using mocked trust bundle.
- Commit 2: integrate validator into KMS request admission path (kms/handler.go). Add RBAC predicate hooks to policy evaluator and a small policy compiler update to accept new predicates.
- Commit 3: audit enrichment and logging changes, add end-to-end tests simulating tenant with EU-only residency. Update docs and add a migration note for operators.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/security/residency/validator.go (new) - implements proof parsing, TTL validation, and signature verification against trust bundle
- pkg/security/residency/validator_test.go (new) - unit tests covering VALID/EXPIRED/INVALID/MISSING cases
- internal/kms/handler.go - wire residency validator into KMS API admission flow (early reject + metrics)
- internal/rbac/predicate.go - add residency predicates and short-circuit logic
- observability/audit/encoder.go - append residency_verification metadata and compact proof reference
- deploy/feature-gates.yaml - add 'residency_proofs' gate and documentation
- docs/security/residency-proofs.md - new operator-facing doc describing proof format, trust bundle rotation, and rollback guidance

Illustrative snippets (small):
- validator.Verify(proofBytes) -> (Outcome, proofRef)
- policy: allow: kms:wrap_key where rbac.residency_allowed == true

Review conversation (highlights, condensed into single thread):
- Leah Kim (reviewer): "This is the right long-term direction. A couple of requests: 1) can we reduce the surface area of the trust bundle API so installers can't accidentally replace it without operator intent? 2) add unit tests for expired proofs with clock skew tolerance."
- Author (Ravi): "Addressed both in commit 2: trust bundle is now provisioned via KMS key manager with an explicit 'trust-bundle' ConfigMap name; added skew tolerance tests (±2m)."
- Anya Sokolov (security): "Please ensure we don't log full proof payloads in any case. The audit encoder looks good but add a unit that asserts sensitive fields are redacted."
- Author: "Added assertions and updated audit encoder to emit only 'proof_ref' and 'validator_version'."
- Diego Martinez (approver): "Verified end-to-end with an EU-only tenant test; performance microbenchmark shows ~0.6ms median overhead on hot-path when proof is cached. Approve pending CI."

CI and flaky runs:
- Initial run: build/presubmit failed on a lint rule (golangci: error on exported doc comment). Fixed in follow-up commit.
- E2E test run: one flaky test in audit-forwarder, rerun passed. Final status: all green.

Operational considerations / rollout plan:
- Feature is behind 'residency_proofs' gate. Operators should enable in canary clusters first. When enabled, the validator will return MISSING for requests without proofs — policy default is to allow, so behavior is non-blocking unless admins explicitly write residency_denied predicates.
- For strict enforcement, customers must: 1) enable feature gate; 2) update RBAC policies to include residency predicates; 3) supply tenant trust bundle via the documented ConfigMap/Secret flow.
- Metrics added: residency_verification_total{outcome=VALID|INVALID|EXPIRED|MISSING} and latency histogram residency_verification_latency_seconds.

Security review notes:
- Signature verification uses tenant-supplied X.509 assertion signed by approved issuers from the trust bundle. Trust bundle rotation is supported and documented.
- We intentionally avoid including full proofs in audit logs to limit exposure. Proof references are sha256(proofBytes) so auditors can request the full proof from the tenant if necessary (out-of-band).

Related work / references:
- ENG-4127: Residency proof design RFC
- SEC-908: KMS geography policy spike
- SUP-2214: Customer ticket for cross-region key usages that motivated this work

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for validator edge cases (malformed, expired, bad signature)
notes: Operator docs and a short migration guide are included in docs/security/residency-proofs.md. This PR is intentionally conservative: no enforcement by default and operator-controlled policy required to block requests.
changelog: Added KMS residency proof validator and residency-aware RBAC predicates behind a feature gate. Operators must opt-in to enforce residency.
